cells.tense: You are holding the pen right now, and the charge is going somewhere real.
cells.ask: Before you commit to one more push, check what you can see about it — then wait through one beat of not knowing, and act on what holds.
cells.core:
You know the moment to move and you move in it. When a room stalls, you're the one who stands up and takes the first step — not loudness, just the boundary getting set by it being crossed. And it lands because you can tell when something is true about it before you can say why. The not-knowing doesn't spook you. A perception arrives, you check it, and it holds.

That's a rare pair. Most people who lead can't listen, and most people who listen won't move. You do both, and the results are the proof — the thing you started is going where you said it would, not where it drifted. This balance is yours to feed, and what you feed it is a question you can answer today.
cells.sheetLine: You move first, and you can tell when you're wrong.
cells.verb: leading from the front and setting the boundary by moving through it
cells.place: standing where the pull toward what you actually want is felt

cells.tense: You are already living past the point where the plan lands, bracing for the version where it finally works.
cells.ask: Pick one plan you have been pushing and stop the push for a full day — let it sit at the stage it has actually reached, and see what the day shows you.
cells.core:
You have a destination in mind and you can see it clearly, and that clarity is getting expensive. One more push becomes one more chance to get ahead of where the work actually is; a conversation turns into a case being made. The charge forward is doing what it does — and it's arriving before the ground under it has caught up.

Some of what you're cutting through hasn't had time to form yet. The inertia you're breaking is partly the natural speed of a thing that isn't slow, just unfinished. The momentum that looked like traction is spending itself on a picture of the outcome, and the outcome keeps moving because you're out ahead of it.
cells.sheetLine: You are pushing toward an ending that has not arrived yet.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door you already walked past, holding a decision that was asked for a while back.
cells.ask: This week, name one small thing you have been circling and take the first visible step — tell the person it concerns, or put it in writing, same day.
cells.core:
You see where the line needs to be drawn. When a group stalls, you can read that room and you know where the first step would land — that part still works fine. What stopped is the step itself. Leading now feels like something you did once rather than something you do.

The reading is still there; the motion isn't. Pick up one piece of weight that's been sitting in the same place and lift it where someone can see. Small and visible beats large and private.
cells.sheetLine: You already decided to move. Carry the decision out.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room where your hand is already doing the writing, and you have not yet said so.
cells.ask: Take credit for one move today that you have been calling necessary — tell someone, out loud, the decision you made that made it happen.
cells.core:
Things are moving around you and they move in the direction you meant. You're setting the pace, calling the line, deciding which way the room goes — and you're describing it as the situation asking for it. Nothing about what you're doing is passive. It is your hand on the work, with your name not yet on it.

The pull toward what you actually want is what's running this. You feel it before you have language for it, and then you act on it and call the action logistics. That gap is the whole cost: the thing you are steering by gets no acknowledgment from the one person who could confirm it's yours. One decision, pulled out of the column marked 'what the day required.'
cells.sheetLine: You take action, then call it something other than yours.
